DecSummary: The worker suffered head and neck injuries in 2011. The Vice-Chair found that the worker did not have entitlement for tinnitus as a separate area of injury. Board policy provides entitlement for tinnitus if there is an accepted claim for noise-induced hearing loss, which was not the situation in this case. The merits and justice can be used to grant entitlement for tinnitus in a situation where a worker has a hearing loss but the hearing loss is not sufficient to meet the requirements for noise-induced hearing loss as required by Board policy. The merits and justice cannot be used to give the worker duplicate entitlement for symptoms that are related to an area of accepted entitlement. In this case, the tinnitus resulted from the worker's head injury, for which he has entitlement. The tinnitus is a symptom of the head injury and not a separate area of entitlement.

The employer's application for reconsideration of certain aspects of Decision No. 1876/17 was granted. The case was a complicated matter involved a volunteer firefighter with concurrent employment. The original vice-chair decided the issue before her, but the reasons provided for the decision were not sufficient to support the conclusion. The worker requested a reconsideration of Decision No. 929/17. As part of the request for reconsideration, the worker had provided new medical reports which were found to be reply evidence, and therefore not admissible for the purposes of a reconsideration. Admitting reply evidence in a reconsideration request would invite ongoing litigation and subvert the finality of decisions.

The Vice-Chair found that there was no fundamental error of law or process made, which if corrected, would likely have produced a different result. The preponderance of evidence did not support a conclusion that the worker's condition related to his compensable workplace accident in 2005. The additional documentation provided by the worker for the reconsideration did not amount to substantial new evidence, particularly the medical reports provided, that had already been in the file and were quoted in the original decision. The threshold test for granting a reconsideration request was not met.
The worker's second application for reconsideration of Decision No. 3824/17 was denied. The original vice-chair considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion.
